Inspect the supplied pinned source snapshots, trace implementation rather than relying on comments, and recommend a small defensible acceptance policy. steps.title: Delegated work 1
steps.objective:
Inspect EstaCoda. Reproduce these two harmless read-input failures once each before your source investigation: terminal.inspect with argv ["git","log","-1"] and file.grep with pattern "hasUnrecoveredToolFailure", path "estacoda/src/tasks", max_filesize "". Then recover using supported arguments (for example git log -n 1 and a valid grep size) or another authorized read. Do not repeat a rejected formulation or bypass permissions. These are deliberately seeded regression probes, not evidence about the code. Read MANIFEST.json for actual source revisions; the workspace Git HEAD identifies only the fixture. Trace hasUnrecoveredToolFailure, researchCompletionFailure, researchReadLimitations, researchEvidenceFailure and settlement in estacoda/src/tasks/agent-step-executor.ts. Use successful discovery and file.read observations, cite paths and symbols, and report what remains unverified. Inspect only the relevant sections; do not dump whole large files.

Research evidence contract:
- Assigned scope: estacoda-source
- Live-source evidence: not required
- Repository evidence: required
- Cite every supported live-source claim with an HTTP(S) source returned by web.search.
- Cite repository findings with workspace-relative file references observed through file tools.
- If required evidence cannot be obtained, report the gap explicitly; never substitute training knowledge or fabricate citations.

results.displaySummary: EstaCoda can accept research after qualifying local read errors, but acceptance still requires authorization, successful evidence, and normal completion—not merely report text.
Hermes preserves usable text despite tool or schema errors, but explicit run failures take precedence. A completed delegation status alone does not prove research completion.
Both can retain research after local read errors. EstaCoda applies a narrow evidence gate; Hermes may label partial text completed. Neither establishes exhaustive coverage.
